question: Should recording publication evidence for an already-published version keep requiring the exact release runtime pin (Node v24.19.0, npm 11.17.0, zlib 1.3.2.1-motley-3246f1b), or should the pin be narrowed to the steps that produce or verify bytes, with evidence recording requiring only a minimum npm version?
options: Keep the exact pin on evidence recording, as before (status quo)
Narrow the pin: keep it exact for every step that produces or verifies bytes, and require only npm major version 11 or newer, checked immediately before npm audit signatures, for evidence recording
Drop every runtime requirement from evidence recording, including the npm floor
recommendation: Option 2, the narrowing that the read-only analysis in foundry issue #1659 supported: the recording path only downloads the published tarball and compares hashes and integrity, reads the archived qualification transcript, and checks git ancestry, so the exact tuple protects nothing there, while npm audit signatures --include-attestations is the one toolchain-sensitive step and needs a recent npm.
decision: On 2026-09-29 the owner delegated this call in chat with the words "make the right pin decision for me, then execute", after the read-only analysis in foundry issue #1659. The master session made the call under that delegation on 2026-09-29, using that analysis: option 2. Narrowed scope: recording publication evidence for an already-published version (createLaterPublicationRecord in scripts/record-later-publication.mjs, reached by the direct join, the v3 replay and the command line) no longer calls assertReleaseRuntime. Instead, immediately before npm audit signatures --include-attestations runs, verifiedAnonymousAudit reads the version of the npm that will run the audit and refuses, with a clear message, unless its major version is 11 or newer, or when the version is unreadable. Both callers of verifiedAnonymousAudit are covered. Unchanged: the exact pin in scripts/lib/release-runtime.mjs remains required, with no change to its values, for qualification (run-candidate-qualification.mjs, candidate-runner.mjs), packing and artifact reproducibility (artifact-reproducibility.mjs), publishing (publish-qualified-directory.mjs, publish-qualified-set.mjs) and retention. The setup-node pin and the assert step in .github/workflows/record-publication-evidence.yml are unchanged, so automated evidence records are still produced on the exact tuple; only a comment there was updated. This decision does not authorize relaxing the pin for any step that produces or verifies bytes.
notes: CHAT CHANNEL, NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIABLE: this record cites an owner chat message and cannot be checked against anything in this repository. THE DECISION WAS DELEGATED, NOT TYPED AS A SPECIFIC OPTION BY THE OWNER: the owner wrote only the delegation quoted in `decision`; the choice of option 2 and its exact scope were made by the master session under that delegation, so `decidedBy: owner` records the delegated authority, not an owner-selected option. The `recommendation` restates the master session's summary of the #1659 analysis and was not independently re-read when this record was written; `reviews` is empty because no reviewer identities were captured for that analysis. JUDGMENT CALLS: (1) `relaxesGateOrPolicy` is true. The change replaces an exact-match refusal on the recording path with a weaker minimum-version check, which loosens an existing check. The argument that the pin never protected anything on this path is plausible but is the kind of self-serving characterization the contract warns about, so the record declares the loosening and lets the sunset bound it. (2) `sunset` and `expiry` are both 2027-03-29, about six months after the decision. The contract forces a non-null sunset and a non-null expiry for a relaxation, so those values are contract-valid rather than derived from any owner-stated duration; the date is the master session's choice of a review interval for the pin's scope. After the sunset, scripts/check-decision-records.mjs flags this record unless a later record whose `supersedes` names it renews the narrowing, or the recorder is reverted to the exact pin. (3) `links.pullRequests` and `links.paths` are empty on purpose. scripts/land-stack.mjs reads decision records from a pull request's base commit, so a record added by the same pull request cannot authorize that pull request, and a pull-request link would also require a pinned patch-id that cannot include the record itself. A path link would pre-authorize future changes to those paths until the expiry. The pull request that adds this record touches tier-2 paths (scripts/lib/release-runtime.mjs and this file), so it needs the owner's own merge under the merge-train gate's report-only or bootstrap handling. `links.issues` names #1659.
